beforeAfter.keys: Keys: 1 to 4 change the comparison, Space switches in Toggle, left and right arrows move the slider, + and - zoom, 0 fits. Drag to pan, double-click to fit.
beforeAfter.differenceNote: |after - before| per pixel, mean {mean} of 255; the scale stops at {top}, where 99 % of the pixels are.
vision.map.building: Building the map of the images
vision.map.buildingWhy: Each image is described once; the map is then saved and opens at once next time. You can use the other tabs meanwhile.
vision.map.by.label: Label
vision.map.none.label: No label
vision.map.deepOffer: describes what images show rather than their colours, and often separates classes better. Its weights ({size}, {licence}) are downloaded once, after you agree (R-VDP-02).
vision.map.confirmBody: {name} needs its weights once: {size}, licence {licence}, from Hugging Face.
vision.map.confirmSafety: The file is checked by its SHA-256 and read as safetensors: no downloaded code is ever run. Nothing is sent about your images.
vision.map.deepWhy: A frozen network describes each image by what it shows rather than by its colours: the map usually separates the classes better. It runs on the graphics card when there is one.
vision.map.axes: The two axes keep {a} % and {b} % of the variance.
vision.map.axesTsne: t-SNE: neighbours stay together, distances between groups mean little.
vision.map.canvasLabel: Map of {points} images, coloured by {by}. The legend lists every colour with its count.
vision.map.how: Hover a point to see it, click to open it. Click a colour to put it forward; the arrow selects all its images. The lasso selects what it surrounds.
vision.map.howTouch: Tap a point to see it and select its group; pinch to zoom.
vision.map.hint: Wheel to zoom: the points become images as you zoom in
vision.map.hintLasso: Draw around the images to select them
vision.map.hintTouch: Pinch to zoom, tap a point
vision.map.advancedHint: t-SNE, HDBSCAN, the number of groups
vision.map.projectionTip: PCA keeps the large distances: two groups far apart are really different. t-SNE keeps the neighbours: tight groups, but the space between them means little. Computed on demand.
vision.map.clusteringTip: k-means makes k round groups, k chosen by the best silhouette from 2 to 12. HDBSCAN finds groups of any shape and leaves isolated images out.
vision.map.silhouetteChart: Silhouette for each number of groups
vision.map.silhouetteSentence: k = {k} gives the best silhouette ({s}); above 0.25 the groups are separate, below they overlap.
vision.prepare.sentence: Images enter the model at {size} × {size} px, {fit}, normalised as ImageNet; {steps}.
vision.prepare.never: Nothing changes your files: the steps run on the fly at training.
vision.prepare.task.classification: Labels found: classification (augmentations by default: flip and crop).
vision.prepare.task.anomaly: Normal images only: anomaly detection, so no augmentation by default (a rotation can be the defect).
vision.prepare.task.clusters: No labels: groups only, no augmentation by default.
vision.prepare.pipeline: Preparation steps, in the order they run
vision.prepare.bordersSuggest: Suggested: many images have a uniform border
vision.prepare.reason.decode: What the eye sees: the camera's orientation applied, transparency flattened on white, the first frame of an animation, 16-bit images brought to 8 bits.
vision.prepare.reason.trim: Scans and screenshots often carry a plain frame: cropping it first means no input pixel is spent on it. Comes before the size step.
vision.prepare.reason.resize: The network reads a square of fixed size (DINOv2: 224, a multiple of 14). Crop keeps the centre at full resolution; pad keeps the whole image on the mean grey. Every later step works at this size, so a setting means the same in the preview and at training.
vision.prepare.reason.white_balance: Gray world: each colour channel is scaled to the same mean. Useful when the lighting differs between images; it can remove a colour that matters.
vision.prepare.reason.denoise: Sensor noise smoothed away. It runs before equalising and sharpening, which would amplify it.
vision.prepare.reason.equalise: Stretches the brightness levels of the luminance only, so colours keep their hue. CLAHE works tile by tile and limits the stretch. Useful in industrial or medical imaging; often harmful on ordinary photos.
vision.prepare.reason.sharpen: Unsharp mask: edges made crisper. It also sharpens noise and compression blocks.
vision.prepare.reason.augment: Random variations seen at training only, never at evaluation, with a fixed seed. Classification: flip and crop by default. Anomalies: none, because a rotated part can be the defect.
vision.prepare.reason.normalise: Every channel centred and scaled with the means and deviations the network was trained with. These are numbers, not a picture: no preview.
vision.prepare.oddRule: An image over 4:1 is padded even in crop mode (R-VPR-04), so nothing is lost.
vision.prepare.anomalyWarning: Anomaly detection: an augmentation can create or hide a defect. Off by default for this task.
vision.prepare.samplesRule: Six images by rule: 2 typical, the lowest and highest {measure} (when they differ), the rest at random.
vision.prepare.samplesAugment: One typical image, six random draws.
vision.prepare.noDifference: Difference is not offered: this step changes the geometry, so pixels no longer match.
vision.prepare.notComparable: Sharpness depends on the image size: not compared across a resize (R-VPR-09).
vision.prepare.normaliseCaption: ImageNet means and standard deviations, per channel (0 to 1 scale)
vision.prepare.normaliseNote: Each pixel becomes (value - mean) / deviation: the padding grey (124, 116, 104) becomes 0.
